answers.Q1: https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/express-checkout-element-link describes Link, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Klarna and Amazon Pay as supported one-click buttons. It describes sorting by customer location, adding supported buttons without frontend changes and reusing an Elements instance (old raw lines 8-17 and new raw lines 9-18). With Stripe.js initialized and a DOM mount target, the unchanged sample calls stripe.elements with payment mode, amount 1099, usd and appearance, creates the expressCheckout instance with options, and mounts it to #express-checkout-element (old raw lines 19-38 and new raw lines 20-35). That is browser UI setup. The sample establishes no customer authentication, backend Session or Intent creation, confirmation, funds availability or settlement. The separate Link integration guide requires enabling Link under Wallets and integrating it, with display for eligible transactions (lines 7-16). The broader Express Checkout Element overview adds active-and-supported method, browser, currency, customer setup where applicable and sandbox/live domain-registration conditions (lines 44-57). source-stripe-express-checkout-link.md lines 13-24 follows the May overview’s sorting, reuse and mount behavior and records its local screenshot. Its six-method count should say six named built-ins. Both captures use an inclusive list and the broader November guide documents customPaymentMethods.
answers.Q2:
https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/express-checkout-element-link shows no substantive change to the documented integration. The copy edit, local image reference becoming a CDN URL, and JavaScript layout, quotes and semicolon changes preserve the same caption and sample operations (old raw lines 12-38 and new raw lines 13-35). The November See also changes Link Authentication Element to Contact Details Element and adds the Express Checkout acceptance guide while keeping the Web Elements and Address Element links (old raw lines 40-44 and new raw lines 37-42). Preserve the 2026-05-08 old raw and asset provenance in source-stripe-express-checkout-link.md. The separate 2026-05-27 Dahlia rename changelog, lines 7-13, says both linkAuthentication and contactDetails remain supported for standard Elements, so the old navigation label and current label can cross-reference each other with dates. Neither field appears in the mount example.

The linked November acceptance base capture gives Checkout Sessions API and Payment Intents API variant navigation. Keep the April 2026 detailed guide’s confirmation flows and optional manual fields attributed to the historical paths, with reciprocal warnings wherever a current recipe would reuse them. Under the corresponding Endive notes, Checkout Session Create and the named Intent writes reject the old server payment_method_types request, and deferred Stripe.js Elements rejects the separate camel-case paymentMethodTypes client option and documents allowedPaymentMethodTypes. The thin Link guide neither ranks the two paths nor specifies a version or either manual field. Keep April’s ready/availablePaymentMethods availability example dated, alongside the broader November overview’s availablepaymentmethodschange/paymentMethods example. The event and mount are UI states, distinct from successful confirmation and settlement. The separate Klarna button also establishes no Klarna funding inside Link on this surface. The US Klarna on Link guide limits that funding path to Payment Links, hosted Checkout and the Payment Element.
